meta.purpose: Seed shortlist for the Altrue MVP prototype. Figures are evaluator estimates, shown exactly as sourced. Every entry has source_url, source_name and an as-of date, per the T-05 provenance rule.
open_questions: Which entries make the featured set (suggested: givedirectly, the four GiveWell-recommended charities, givewell-top-charities-fund, one animal fund, globalgiving-projects).
Tax deductibility for a Germany-based tester is not verified. Do not show any tax claim until it is sourced.
GlobalGiving API key approval, rate limits and terms of use still need checking before building the live feed.
ACE list header reads 2025; ACE page was modified 2026-11-04. Re-check before any public launch.
Marianne van der Werf talk on effectiveness.org is from 2020 and names older ACE picks (Anima International, FIAPO). It was used as background only, not as a current list.

entries.name: GiveDirectly
entries.region: Kenya, Uganda, Rwanda, Malawi, DRC, Mozambique, US
entries.summary: Sends cash straight to people living in extreme poverty by mobile money, no strings attached. Recipients choose how to spend it.

key_figures.label: of funds directly delivered to people in need
key_figures.basis: GiveDirectly homepage headline; the site also says more than 87% for its flagship program

key_figures.label: lower infant mortality in a Kenya randomised study of $1,000 transfers
key_figures.basis: As reported by GiveDirectly on its own site

entries.evidence: Cash transfers are heavily studied (GiveDirectly cites 1,000+ studies). Long-term effects and spillovers are still being researched.
entries.evaluator: GiveWell (top charity 2012 to 2022, not on the current list); Charity Navigator 99% four-star; CharityWatch Top Rated (as shown by GiveDirectly)
entries.source_name: GiveDirectly homepage; GiveWell GiveDirectly review page
entries.notes: Honesty note: GiveWell removed GiveDirectly from its top charities list in Aug 2022 after changing its criteria, and says this did not reflect a change in its view of the program. GiveWell says it still has a very high view of GiveDirectly. Monthly giving is offered. Strong candidate for the featured anchor.

entries.name: GiveWell Top Charities Fund
entries.summary: One gift that GiveWell grants to the top charities it thinks will help most, at zero fees. You are told which programs it chose.
entries.source_name: GiveWell Our Top Charities (last updated Oct 2026)
entries.notes: Good fit for the 'let experts decide' option in the split preview.

entries.name: GiveWell All Grants Fund
entries.summary: Supports a wider range of global health programs, including newer or higher-risk projects that could become future top charities.
entries.evidence: Wider and less certain than the Top Charities Fund (per Giving What We Can's description).
entries.evaluator: GiveWell; listed by Giving What We Can
entries.source_name: Giving What We Can Best Charities (2026)
entries.notes: GiveWell lists the fund on its own site; the description here comes from Giving What We Can.

entries.name: EA Funds Animal Welfare Fund
entries.summary: Backs promising ways to reduce farmed animal suffering, from corporate advocacy to alternative protein research.

key_figures.label: can protect dozens or hundreds of farmed and aquatic animals
key_figures.basis: Giving What We Can claim; method not shown on the page

entries.evidence: Giving What We Can recommends it, based on its evaluator research.
entries.source_name: Giving What We Can Best Charities (2026)
entries.notes: Treat the $10 figure as 'illustrative' until the method is sourced.

entries.name: Effective Animal Advocacy Fund (Giving What We Can)
entries.summary: Splits one gift between the EA Funds Animal Welfare Fund and the Animal Charity Evaluators Movement Grants program.
entries.evidence: Allocations set by Giving What We Can's research team.
entries.source_name: Giving What We Can Best Charities (2026)

entries.name: Risks and Resilience Fund (Giving What We Can)
entries.summary: Funds projects that cut risks from pandemics, nuclear threats and AI, run by expert grantmakers.
entries.evidence: Hard-to-measure, high-stakes area; allocations set by Giving What We Can's research team.
entries.source_name: Giving What We Can Best Charities (2026)

entries.name: The Humane League
entries.summary: Campaigns to get companies to drop the worst confinement practices for farmed chickens, and supports groups worldwide through the Open Wing Alliance.
entries.evidence: High cost effectiveness through corporate commitments (ACE assessment). Recommended by ACE since 2014.

entries.name: Shrimp Welfare Project
entries.region: Central and South America, Southeast Asia, India
entries.summary: Works with shrimp farmers on humane stunning, better water quality and lower stocking density.
entries.evidence: Exceptionally cost effective through direct work with the industry (ACE assessment). Recommended by ACE since 2023.

entries.name: Sinergia Animal
entries.region: Latin America, Ecuador, Indonesia, Peru, Thailand (as listed by ACE)
entries.summary: Runs corporate outreach and meat-reduction programs to improve conditions for farmed chickens and pigs.
entries.evidence: High cost effectiveness (ACE assessment). Recommended by ACE since 2018.

entries.name: Wild Animal Initiative
entries.summary: Builds the science of wild animal welfare through grants, research and academic outreach.
entries.evidence: Potential to affect very large numbers of animals by speeding up research; earlier-stage than the other animal picks (ACE assessment). Recommended by ACE since 2020.

entries.name: GlobalGiving vetted local projects
entries.impact_area: Community-chosen (education, gender equality, climate, food security, health)
entries.summary: A platform of vetted local projects. Altrue can pull live projects through the GlobalGiving API instead of hard-coding them.
entries.evidence: GlobalGiving's site shows 'Most Effective' and 'Site Visit Verified' filters. Project-level quality varies, so show these labels and not a score.
entries.evaluator: GlobalGiving (Charity Navigator four-star, Candid Platinum, BBB Accredited, as shown on its site)
entries.notes: API: REST, uses an api_key query parameter (example on the getting-started page). Key approval, rate limits and terms of use not checked yet. No individual projects are listed here on purpose; fetch them at runtime and keep the source URL on each.
